item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM): how to turn your documents into notes, quizzes and audio","dek":"How to set up a notebook, ask questions about your own files, and use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026, but it still works the same way: you add your own sources and it answers and builds study material from them. Here is how to use each part, step by step, and where it falls short.","seo_title":"Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) Guide: Notes, Quizzes, Audio","seo_description":"How to use Gemini Notebook, formerly NotebookLM: add sources, ask cited questions, make Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and study guides.","answer_summary":"Create a notebook, add your sources (PDFs, Docs, slides, audio, links or YouTube videos), ask questions in the chat, then use the Studio panel to generate Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes, reports and more from those sources.","tags":["Gemini Notebook","NotebookLM","Google","Studying","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM, Google's research and study tool. Google announced the rename on July 16, 2026, and said the product stays a standalone research tool. The idea has not changed: you give it your own material, such as lecture notes, PDFs or a recorded talk, and it answers questions and builds study aids from that material instead of from the open web. This guide covers how to set up a notebook, how to ask good questions, and how to use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you used NotebookLM before, nothing breaks. Google's Workspace team said automatic redirects keep existing shared notebooks and links working, and the new name and logo appear across the product over several weeks. On mobile you may need to update the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Set up your first notebook","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create a notebook","text":"Open Gemini Notebook in your browser and select Create new notebook. In the window that opens, choose Upload a source. Use one notebook per subject or project. Each notebook is separate, and Gemini Notebook cannot pull information from several notebooks at once, so a notebook for your biology class will not know what is in your history notebook.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add the right sources","text":"Select Add sources on the left. Gemini Notebook accepts PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, Google Sheets, Word, PowerPoint, TXT, Markdown, CSV and ePub files, images, audio files such as MP3 and WAV, pasted text, web links, public YouTube videos and Gemini chats. Each source can hold up to 500,000 words, or 200 MB for an uploaded file, and free users can add up to 50 sources per notebook. Sources from Google Drive sync automatically, but footnotes and comments in those files are not imported.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"No material yet: type a question into the search box in the Sources panel and pick Web or Drive. Gemini Notebook shows results you can import. Turn on Deep Research for a longer search that takes a few minutes; Google says that option is only for users over 18.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask questions about your own files","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Once sources are in, the chat panel shows a summary of them and suggested questions. Answers draw on the notebook's sources and include citations that link back to the passage they came from, according to Layer3Labs' walkthrough. You can also switch individual sources off in the Sources panel to narrow what an answer uses.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Find what matters for the test","text":"Using only my sources, explain [topic] in plain words. Then list the 5 facts I am most likely to be tested on, and point to where each one appears.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Spot the gaps","text":"Compare what [source 1] and [source 2] say about [topic]. List where they agree, where they disagree, and anything one covers that the other leaves out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Click the citations on anything you plan to quote or memorize. The answer is only as good as the passage behind it, and checking takes seconds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turn your notes into a podcast","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews live in the Studio panel. Google's help center lists four formats: Deep Dive, the default, where two hosts discuss your sources; The Brief, one speaker giving the key points in under two minutes; The Critique, two hosts giving feedback on something like an essay; and The Debate, two hosts arguing different sides. You can choose Shorter, Default or Longer, though Longer works in English only. More than 80 languages are supported.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Generate an Audio Overview with a focus","text":"In Studio, open Audio Overview, pick a format and length, and add a prompt that says what to focus on and how expert the listener is. It generates in the background, which can take a couple of minutes, so you can keep working. You can download the audio when it is done.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A beginner's audio lesson","text":"Focus only on [chapter or topic]. Explain it for a beginner, use one everyday example per idea, and end with the 3 points I must remember.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is also an Interactive mode. When you create a new Audio Overview with it switched on, you can select Join while listening and ask the hosts a question by voice; they answer from your sources and then carry on. Google says it is English only, works only on newly generated overviews, and may have delays or audio glitches.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Quiz yourself with flashcards and quizzes","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Customize before you generate","text":"In Studio, select Flashcards or Quizzes to generate right away, or click the pencil icon first to customize. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more items, and add a prompt about the topic, audience or style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Questions that test understanding","text":"Make questions only about [topic]. Mix definitions with questions that ask me to apply an idea to a new example. Skip anything not in my sources.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"While you study, the Explain button gives the reasoning behind a card or an answer. On flashcards you mark each card Got it! or Missed it!, and Gemini Notebook saves your progress. At the end you can practice again with the same cards, all cards, or only the ones you missed. Flashcards can be downloaded as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build study guides and reports","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel also makes notes, Video Overviews, mind maps, data tables, slide decks, infographics and reports. Report types include a study guide, a briefing document, an FAQ or a custom report, and a report can be exported to Google Docs from its three dot menu. Edits you make in the exported Doc do not sync back to the notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A one page study guide","text":"Create a one page study guide on [topic]: key terms with short definitions, a timeline of the main events, and 5 practice questions with answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gemini Notebook is only as good as what you put in. If your sources are thin or wrong, its answers and quizzes will be too, and it will not tell you what your notes are missing unless you ask. Google itself warns that Audio Overviews are AI generated and can contain inaccuracies, so treat them as a way to review, not as the final word. It also cannot combine notebooks, and the mobile app may not support every feature. For a quick fact check against the open web, a search tool is still the better fit; for learning a specific set of material well, this is the tool to use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free accounts get the core features. Google's paid AI plans raise the limits on notebooks, sources and daily generations, and some newer features, such as code that runs inside a notebook to analyze data, started with Google AI Ultra users before a wider rollout.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]}]}

item.title: Anthropic just made $17 billion in three months. It still lost money
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows $17 billion in revenue for July to September, up from $11.6 billion in the second quarter. A year earlier, the same quarter brought in about $1.4 billion. Price cuts and discounts took about $600 million off revenue. Operating costs jumped to $17.5 billion from $10.6 billion, turning a $974 million profit into a $567 million loss. Short-term compute cost $5 billion, far more than multi-year deals, Anthropic says. A $2 billion non-cash charge for donation matching also hit. Sources: Fortune, Analytics India Magazine, Investing.com.

item.title: Anthropic wants $3.5 billion from Japan before its stock even starts trading
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Japanese filing shows Anthropic plans to sell up to 552.9 billion yen of shares to investors in Japan, Reuters reported on November 2. The money goes to working capital, operating costs and capital spending. That is a ceiling, not a final allocation. In SpaceX's June IPO, the largest ever, investors in Japan secured $2.2 billion of the $75 billion raised. Anthropic's Japan ceiling is about 1.6 times that amount. Anthropic filed on October 26 to list on Nasdaq as ANT. Share count and price range are not set. Sources: Reuters, FourWeekMBA, Anthropic.

item.title: The best AI model just took a test of real expert work. It scored 12%
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: SemiAnalysis released GDPx on November 2: 206 tasks in 11 fields, from chip design and cybersecurity to finance, law and biology. Each task can run up to 8 hours in a realistic work setup built with specialist partner companies. The GDPx V1.0 leaderboard Claude Opus 5.5 led with 12.0%. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon was second at 10.9% and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra third at 9.6%. Gemini cost $16.29 per task. Claude cost $51.41. Score vs cost per task Graded as pass or fail, every model scored zero on the finance and legal tasks. Sources: SemiAnalysis, Unite.AI, OfficeChai.

Tasks have a default time limit of eight hours, and models run in their own tools where available: Claude Code for Opus 5.5, Codex for GPT-6 Astra and Antigravity for Gemini 4 Carbon.","sources":[{"name":"SemiAnalysis","url":"https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The headline score averages each model's pass@1 result over three attempts, with every field weighted equally. SemiAnalysis called GDPx a true frontier benchmark because even the best model reaches only 12%. The firm plans new versions every three to six months.","sources":[{"name":"SemiAnalysis","url":"https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the models struggled","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Finance and legal tasks proved so hard under binary grading that every model scored zero, so SemiAnalysis also reported partial scores. On legal partial scores, Opus 5.5 averaged 44% and GPT-6 Astra 25%. In quant trading, 70 of 111 graded runs did worse than the reference strategy, and none of the 12 attempts at one hardware design task produced a verified full pass.","sources":[{"name":"SemiAnalysis","url":"https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Results varied widely by field. SemiAnalysis named Opus 5.5 the best all-around model, with wins in quant trading, hardware design and chip design. Gemini 4 Carbon was the strongest biology model, GPT-6 Astra led recursive self-improvement and materials science, and Meta's Muse Wonder Full was described as the best cyber model by a meaningful margin.","sources":[{"name":"SemiAnalysis","url":"https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Cost also differed sharply. Opus 5.5 cost $51.41 per task and GPT-6 Astra $53.99, while Gemini 4 Carbon cost $16.29, according to Unite.AI.","sources":[{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/"},{"name":"OfficeChai","url":"https://officechai.com/ai/claude-opus-5-5-tops-semi-analysis-gdpx-benchmark-gemini-4-carbon-placed-second/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The safety filter effect","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SemiAnalysis said the overall scores of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are held down by their safety classifiers in cybersecurity, biology and alignment tasks. With those three fields removed, GPT-6 Astra edges Opus 5.5 by 0.1 percentage points and Gemini 4 Carbon drops from second to fifth. The firm said this adjusted ranking better matches its own assessment of the models.","sources":[{"name":"SemiAnalysis","url":"https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities"},{"name":"OfficeChai","url":"https://officechai.com/ai/claude-opus-5-5-tops-semi-analysis-gdpx-benchmark-gemini-4-carbon-placed-second/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The low ceiling is the main takeaway. Labs often promote high scores on older tests, but GDPx shows the strongest models still finish only a small share of long, realistic expert tasks. The cost gap also matters for companies choosing a model, since Gemini 4 Carbon came close to the leader at roughly a third of the price per task.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next GDPx update, expected within three to six months, will show whether new model releases can move the top score meaningfully above 12%.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI doesn't want you to say data center anymore. Here's the new name
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI wants to replace the term data center with AI compute campus. A spokesperson confirmed it to Business Insider on November 1. item.title: Grok Bot users ran out of usage in days. Elon Musk says it was costing too much
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Grok Bot subscribers said this week that their usage ran out much earlier than expected. One user said usage hit 100% with four days left before the weekly reset. Asked on X on November 1 if usage could be reset, Musk said the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue. He gave no figures and did not say if limits will change. xAI launched Grok Bot in early beta in August. It runs research, writing and browsing tasks on its own virtual computer. Sources: Tesla North, Yeni Safak (Anadolu Agency), explainx.ai.

item.title: 8 AI words everyone is suddenly using, and what they actually mean
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: An agent is an AI that runs its own loop: it picks a tool, checks the result and decides the next step. Anthropic separates agents from workflows, where the steps are fixed in code ahead of time. Sources: Anthropic: Building effective agents, Addy Osmani: Agent harness engineering, Anthropic: Introducing the Model Context Protocol, Anthropic: Equipping agents with Agent Skills, arXiv: GEO, Generative Engine Optimization, Conductor: Answer engine optimization, OpenAI Charter, Wikipedia: Superintelligence.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Eight AI terms explained: agents, harnesses, MCP, skills, GEO, AEO, AGI and superintelligence","dek":"A plain reference to the words behind AI tools, AI search and the long term goals of the largest labs, based on the documents that define them.","summary":"Agents, harnesses, MCP and skills describe how AI models use tools and carry out tasks, while GEO and AEO describe how content gets surfaced in AI answers. AGI and superintelligence name the goals that OpenAI, Meta and others say they are working toward.","seo_title":"AI terms explained: agents, MCP, skills, GEO, AGI and more","seo_description":"What agents, harnesses, MCP, skills, GEO, AEO, AGI and superintelligence mean, explained from the documents that define each term.","answer_summary":"An agent is an AI system that directs its own tool use, a harness is the software around a model, MCP is an open standard for connecting AI to data, and skills are folders of instructions an agent loads when needed. GEO and AEO are about being cited in AI answers, and AGI and superintelligence describe AI that matches or far exceeds human ability.","tags":["AI agents","MCP","Agent Skills","GEO","AGI","Superintelligence"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic described AI agents in a December 19, 2024 research post as systems in which large language models direct their own processes and decide how to use tools. The company said agents are usually language models that call tools in a loop and adjust based on feedback from their environment. It set them apart from workflows, in which a model and its tools follow paths that developers write in code ahead of time.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Building effective agents","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How AI gets things done: harnesses, MCP and skills","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A harness is the layer that turns a model into a working agent. In an April 19, 2026 essay, engineer and author Addy Osmani defined it as all of the code, configuration and execution logic that is not the model itself. That covers system prompts and rule files, tool definitions, the loop that runs the agent, context management, memory files, sandboxes and approval gates. Osmani named Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider and Cline as examples, and wrote that the behavior users see depends heavily on the harness even when the underlying model is the same.","sources":[{"name":"Addy Osmani: Agent harness engineering","url":"https://addyosmani.com/blog/agent-harness-engineering/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Model Context Protocol, or MCP, is an open standard that Anthropic introduced on November 25, 2024 for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data is stored. Developers expose data or tools through an MCP server, and AI applications connect to it as clients. At launch, Anthropic published ready made servers for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres and Puppeteer, and named Block, Apollo, Zed, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph among early adopters.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing the Model Context Protocol","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent Skills, which Anthropic announced on October 16, 2025, are organized folders of instructions, scripts and resources. Each skill is a directory with a SKILL.md file that begins with a short block of metadata, including a name and a description. Claude loads only that name and description at the start, reads the full file when a task calls for the skill, and opens any linked files only if they are needed. Anthropic calls this layered approach progressive disclosure and says it keeps skills from filling the model's context.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Equipping agents with Agent Skills","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The four terms fit together. The model does the reasoning, the harness runs it, MCP connects it to outside apps and data, and skills give it task specific know how without loading everything at once. Osmani argues that much of what separates one coding assistant from another sits in those outer layers rather than in the model alone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How content shows up in AI answers: GEO and AEO","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Generative engine optimization, or GEO, was introduced in a November 2023 paper by researchers from Princeton University and the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. The authors described generative engines as search systems that use AI models to gather and summarize information in answer to a query, and proposed GEO as a way for content creators to improve how visible their content is in those answers. They reported that GEO methods could raise visibility by up to 40 percent in generative engine responses.","sources":[{"name":"arXiv: GEO, Generative Engine Optimization","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Answer engine optimization, or AEO, is a closely related idea. The search marketing company Conductor describes it as structuring content so that AI engines can understand it and use it as a direct answer, in tools such as ChatGPT and Perplexity and in formats such as Google's AI Overviews and featured snippets. Conductor says the goal differs from traditional search engine optimization, which focuses on ranking positions, because AEO aims to be cited as the source of the answer.","sources":[{"name":"Conductor: Answer engine optimization","url":"https://www.conductor.com/academy/glossary/answer-engine-optimization/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the labs say this is heading: AGI and superintelligence","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's charter defines artificial general intelligence, or AGI, as highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work, and states that the company's mission is to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity. Superintelligence describes a further step. Wikipedia defines it as a hypothetical agent with intelligence beyond the most gifted human minds and cites philosopher Nick Bostrom's definition of an intellect that greatly exceeds human cognitive performance in virtually all domains. Ilya Sutskever's startup Safe Superintelligence focuses only on building a safe superintelligence, and Meta created a division called Meta Superintelligence Labs in 2025.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Charter","url":"https://openai.com/charter/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Superintelligence","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The first six terms describe tools and practices that exist today and can be tested. AGI and superintelligence are different: they are goals and definitions for systems that do not exist yet, which makes claims about them harder to check.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch how vendors use these words in product launches. A claim about an agent, a skill or an MCP connector can be checked against the published definitions, while a claim about AGI depends on whose definition is being used.","sources":[]}]}

This guide covers how to ask, how to pick sources, how to check the citations, and when to use Research mode and Projects.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a narrow question","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity handles plain, conversational questions, but specific questions get better answers. Keep digging in the same thread","text":"Ask your follow ups as replies in the same thread instead of starting a new search. Perplexity keeps the earlier questions in context, so you can go from a broad overview to one specific detail in a few steps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose where it searches","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The search box has a sources menu that sets where Perplexity looks. Separate strong evidence from early or small studies, and say where the studies disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Social when you want real experiences, like how owners feel about a product after a year. Treat those answers as opinions, not facts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Check the citations","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Each answer has numbered citations, and clicking one opens the original page. item.title: Critics say Apple is losing the AI race. Its new CEO says he likes where they're at
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Apple CEO John Ternus told WIRED's Steven Levy that Apple is "absolutely going to leverage AI" in its products. Then he drew a line: "We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake." Done right, he said, "people won't have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen." Asked if AI agents could replace apps, he said creating products is "a deeply human and personal thing." Ternus, 51, has run Apple since early September after 25 years at the company. Tim Cook is now executive chairman. Sources: ShiftDelete.Net, DigitalToday.

item.description: Starting in December, Plus, Pro and Business plans will share one usage allowance across ChatGPT and Codex, OpenAI's help center says. OpenAI has not given an exact date. Add knowledge files","text":"Under Knowledge, click Add files, then choose Upload files for something on your computer or Drive for a file in Google Drive. A style guide, a price list or a set of past examples works well here. If you do not want the Gem to cite these files in its answers, select Disable knowledge citations.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Preview, then save","text":"Type a test request in the preview panel on the right. The preview does not save anything, so adjust the instructions until the answers look right, then click Save. The three dot menu has Make a copy, which also works on Google's premade Gems.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A writing editor Gem","text":"You are a careful editor for [my newsletter / my work emails].
When I paste a draft, fix grammar and spelling, cut filler words and keep my voice.
Do not add new facts or change numbers.
Return the edited text first, then a short list of the three biggest changes you made.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gems have real limits. According to Zapier, they cannot be used with Gemini Live, they do not take actions outside the chat window, and they cannot use connected apps. So a Gem is best for repeated writing, editing and planning tasks, not for anything that needs your inbox or calendar.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: what Gemini can read","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini web app, click the Add files button below the text box. Upload takes a file from your device and Add from Drive takes one from Google Drive. Under More Uploads you can also import a code folder or a GitHub repository. According to Google, most file types are supported and you can add up to 10 files in the same prompt. Videos can be up to 2 GB each and most other files up to 100 MB.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Length limits depend on the plan. Google says the total video length is up to 5 minutes, or up to 1 hour with Google AI Pro or Ultra, and the total audio length is up to 10 minutes, or up to 3 hours on those plans. One code folder or GitHub repository can be added per chat, with up to 5,000 files and 100 MB. Upload limits are rolling, so if you hit one, you may have to wait before uploading more.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Get the useful part of a long PDF","text":"Read the attached file.
1. Summarize it in five bullet points.
2. List every deadline, date and number that I need to act on, with the page it appears on.
3. Tell me what is missing or unclear.
Only use what is in the file. If something is not in it, say so.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google warns that very large uploads can lead to answers that miss details or connections across the content. If you need precise answers, upload fewer files at once and ask about one document at a time. If Gemini clearly misreads a file, upload it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gmail, Drive and Calendar: ask about your own stuff","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Google Workspace app connects Gemini to your Gmail, Docs and Drive for summaries and lookups, to Google Tasks and Google Keep for reminders, notes and lists, and to Google Calendar for events. To point Gemini at one service, type @ and pick it from the list. Google says to use keywords from the content rather than pasting a link to an email or a document.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Connect Google Workspace","text":"Sign in to Gemini with the same account you use for Gmail and Drive. Keep Activity must be on, or Gemini cannot connect. In Gmail, the setting Smart features in other Google products also has to be on; after you turn it on, reload Gemini. Work and school accounts need the administrator to allow the connection first. To disconnect later, use the Connected Apps settings page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Clear your inbox backlog","text":"@Gmail Find emails from the last 7 days that ask me to reply, decide or send something.
For each one, give me the sender, what they need and by when.
Sort them by deadline, soonest first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Prepare for a meeting","text":"@Google Calendar What is my next meeting with [name]?
@Drive Find the latest documents that mention [project].
Give me a five line briefing: what the meeting is about, what changed since we last met, and two questions I should ask.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The limits matter here. Google lists them plainly: Gemini cannot see comments or images inside Docs and Gmail, or pictures and videos in Drive. It cannot create folders or move files in Drive, cannot count items in Drive or Gmail, and cannot report your storage. In a new chat, name the service in your first prompt; follow up questions in the same chat do not need it. Zapier adds that the list of connected apps and their availability varies by country.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"},{"name":"Zapier: Gemini connected apps","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/gemini-connected-apps/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The Workspace connection is the most useful of the three for busy people, and also the one that needs the most checking. Google itself notes that Gemini can hallucinate or give outdated information here, so open the emails and files it cites before you act on a summary.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where to start","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start with one Gem for the task you repeat most, such as editing emails. Use uploads when you have one long document to understand. Turn on the Workspace connection when you spend too long searching your own inbox, and always check the sources it shows.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: The company that hunts crypto hackers just got hacked with AI agents
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Chainalysis says an outside attacker used "offensive agentic techniques" to get into its systems and internal tools. Exposed: user IDs, full names, emails and role labels. Case files, passwords and login codes show no sign of access. The firm works for banks, exchanges and government agencies. It has not said how the AI agents worked or how much a human steered them. Now it is using AI models to hunt for its own weak spots. Sources: CoinPaprika, The Currency Analytics.

item.title: Hackers built malware that asks Claude what you're worth
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman detailed VOLTA on October 31. It is a Windows stealer that bundles a victim's data and sends it to an AI model. The prompt asks for a target assessment: what the victim is worth. The default model is Claude Opus 4.6, reached through OpenRouter. If the reply contains phrases like "I can't", the malware switches to Moonshot's Kimi K2, then Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash. With no API key it skips the AI step. Sources: Data Studios, Startup Fortune, Sansser.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A man in a hoodie at a cluttered desk with credit cards and a laptop showing an orange logo.

item.title: Sam Altman just flew to Korea to meet 50 Samsung executives as AI memory runs short
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Altman met about 50 senior Samsung leaders in Yongin on Saturday, from its electronics, finance and biotech arms. Samsung said they discussed where AI is heading. He also gave its AI Center head a Codex Micro Keyboard. In October 2025, Samsung signed on as a memory partner for Stargate, OpenAI's data center buildout. Back then, Samsung said OpenAI expected to need up to 900,000 DRAM wafers a month. No new supply deal came out of Saturday's talks. Source: Samsung Newsroom Sources: Tom's Hardware, NewsBytes, Samsung Newsroom.
